concept: A scoreboard that stops moving. The whole story is one number frozen while three wickets fall, so the design leans on repetition: the hero puts '110 for 1. Cruising.' in muted grey and 'Then 110 for 4.' in white, the score unchanged but the wickets column jumping. Slide 2 is a single giant 0, the runs New Zealand added during the collapse. Slide 3 is a fall-of-wickets bar chart where three bars end at exactly the same length, so you see the stall before you read it. Slides 4 and 5 explain why (Gill bowling first on a green pitch, the debutant striking before lunch) and what's at stake in a series decider. Cricket blue, type and charts only: no player photos, no logos.
caption:
110 for 1. Then 110 for 4.

New Zealand were cruising on day 1 of the Christchurch Test. Latham had 59 and the openers had put on 77. Then India took three wickets without conceding a run.

Akash Deep had Latham caught behind by Pant. Kamboj had Nicholls caught at long leg. Akash Deep came back to remove Ravindra for a nine-ball duck, again caught by Pant.

Shubman Gill won the toss and bowled first on a green pitch. Debutant Gurnoor Brar, India's 321st Test player, had already struck with the last ball before lunch when Conway was lbw for 31.

Wellington was a draw, so this Test decides the series. The match is still going on as you read this.
